If you’re not booking through hotel loyalty programs, you’re leaving money on the table. These programs offer cash discounts, free upgrades, complimentary breakfast, access to exclusive lounges and even free nights once you accumulate enough points. Now the question is, which hotel program should you invest in?

In this guide, we'll cover the top hotel rewards programs and help you decide which one(s) suit your travel needs.

Related: The best hotel loyalty programs for families

There are many factors to consider when choosing a hotel rewards program, including:

Let's dive into the pros and cons of each program.

Marriott's impressive portfolio features more than 10,000 properties across 30-plus brands and 140-plus countries and territories, ranging from basic business hotels to safari camps and cabins. No matter where you’re going, there’s bound to be a Marriott nearby.

A key perk of the Marriott Bonvoy program is its fifth-night-free benefit: When redeeming points for five or more consecutive nights, you’ll receive the lowest-priced night for free. This can save you a ton of points, especially if you book an award stay in a high-end destination like the Maldives.

And with several Marriott credit cards and three major 1:1 transfer partners — American Express Membership Rewards, Bilt Points and Chase Ultimate Rewards — it's easy to earn the points you need for your next redemption.

You can get even more from the Bonvoy program if you reach one of its five elite status tiers. Benefits include room upgrades, lounge access and Nightly Upgrade Awards (formerly Suite Night Awards).

Another notable benefit is that members can transfer Bonvoy points to dozens of airline partners, including some with hard-to-earn currencies.

Marriott Bonvoy is good for travelers who:

Related: Your complete guide to earning Marriott Bonvoy points

With over 9,400 properties and 28 brands in 144 countries and territories, Hilton can give Marriott a run for its money. Couple its size with the relative effortlessness of earning Hilton Honors points, and the Hilton Honors program may be the most all-around convenient hotel rewards option.

Like Marriott, Hilton offers the fifth consecutive award night free — but you must have at least Hilton Honors Silver elite status to unlock this benefit. Thankfully, you can achieve this simply by holding any Hilton credit card. Some cards also offer valuable free night certificates or statement credits.

Hilton is an Amex Membership Rewards transfer partner with a handy 1:2 ratio, meaning you'll get 2 Hilton Honors points for every Amex point you transfer (or more if you find a transfer bonus). You can also transfer Bilt Points to Hilton, though at a lower 1:1 ratio.

Related: How much value does the Hilton Honors program provide when you book directly?

World of Hyatt has long been a favorite at TPG, largely because it still uses an award chart and has relatively cheap award rates compared to other hotel programs, even after recent devaluations. For example, standard rooms at Hyatt’s most upscale hotels (excluding all-inclusive resorts, Miraval resorts and Mr & Mrs Smith properties) top out at 75,000 points per night, while a luxury Hilton property could cost up to a whopping 250,000 points.

The downside is that Hyatt offers a relatively small footprint. Hyatt operates 1,500-some hotels (and a few glamping sites) across more than 80 countries, but most are in popular destinations and cities. If you often visit rural areas, World of Hyatt points may not serve you as well.

Plus, since World of Hyatt currently offers only two cobranded credit cards, points aren’t quite as easy to accrue as in some competitor programs. (Though Hyatt has teased that additional cobranded cards may come as part of its expanding partnership with Chase.)

Members of Bilt and Chase Ultimate Rewards can transfer points to World of Hyatt, with a 1:1 ratio for Bilt and either 1:1 or 4:3 for Chase, depending on which credit card you have.

TPG staff members and readers have repeatedly stated that earning Hyatt Globalist status is the most valuable hotel elite status. With free breakfast, waived resort and parking fees on award nights, consistent suite upgrades and more, this status is about as close to a VIP experience as you can get in the hospitality world.

World of Hyatt is good for travelers who:

Related: World of Hyatt elite status: What it is and how to earn it

There’s arguably no better hotel program for stays in small-town America than Wyndham Rewards. The program encompasses over 8,000 hotels across 25 brands, many of which are budget brands — such as Super 8, Days Inn and Microtel — ubiquitous in areas where you won’t find a Hyatt or Marriott. If your travel goals involve getting off the beaten path or road-tripping through towns with populations under 10,000, the Wyndham Rewards program is a great one to focus on.

Unfortunately, Wyndham's loyalty program took a hit when members lost the ability to redeem Wyndham points for Vacasa vacation rentals, a benefit that had previously offered great value. It also suffered a devaluation in 2026 when it introduced a fourth award tier, increasing the maximum redemption from 30,000 points to 45,000 points per night.

Wyndham offers three cobranded credit cards, all issued by Barclays, to help you earn free nights. Additionally, you can transfer Bilt points, Capital One miles, Citi ThankYou Rewards and Chase Ultimate Rewards to Wyndham Rewards at a 1:1 ratio.

Wyndham Rewards is good for travelers who:

Related: How to earn Wyndham points for your next redemption

IHG One Rewards points are easy to earn, and IHG has properties in almost as many locations as Hilton, including some sought-after Six Senses resorts that are bookable with IHG points.

IHG offers three cobranded credit cards, which were revamped in 2026 with new benefits, more ways to earn elite status and, in some cases, higher annual fees. Unfortunately, starting in 2027, cardholders will need to spend $5,000 in a calendar year to unlock the card's fourth-night-free perk, which used to come free with any IHG card. Still, if you meet the spend threshold, this perk is unique among loyalty programs and a better value than Marriott and Hilton’s fifth-night-free policies.

You can transfer Chase Ultimate Rewards points and Bilt points to IHG One Rewards at a 1:1 ratio, though you can often buy IHG points at a steep discount, which could be a better option.

IHG One Rewards offers a solid elite status program, and elite members can earn Milestone Rewards — like an annual lounge membership, bonus points and confirmed suite upgrades — by staying a certain number of nights in a calendar year.

IHG One Rewards is good for travelers who:

Related: How to maximize redemptions with the IHG One Rewards program

Points in the ALL Accor program are the most valuable — and straightforward — of all the major hotel rewards currencies. For every 1,000 points you redeem, you’ll get 20 euros (roughly $25 at the time of writing) off your hotel bill. That comes out to a value of over 2 cents per point, higher than any other hotel currency.

Although the simplicity of this program may appeal to many travelers, there are two areas in which ALL underdelivers: The vast majority of its nearly 6,000 properties are concentrated in Europe and Asia, and it does not offer a cobranded credit card to help you earn points quickly.

Additionally, while ALL Accor has several major transfer partners, all offer a less-than-ideal transfer ratio: 3:2 for Bilt, 2:1 for Capital One and Citi, and 1.5:1 for Rove Miles.

Still, Accor can be a great place to earn hotel points if you primarily travel in Asia or Europe.

The program has four levels of elite status, with top-tier Diamond offering free breakfast on weekends (or every day in the Asia-Pacific region), Suite Night Upgrades and executive lounge access. You’ll also find brand-specific benefits at each status tier, such as complimentary bike rentals at Fairmont properties.

Accor Live Limitless is good for travelers who:

Related: Accor’s first Orient Express train through Italy now open for reservations

With nearly 7,500 properties in over 50 countries, including Radisson Rewards Americas hotels, Choice’s footprint rivals that of better-known loyalty programs like Hilton and Marriott. However, the Choice Privileges program can serve you similarly to Wyndham Rewards in that its participating hotels are more prolific in smaller towns.

Choice Privileges is famously valuable for anyone staying in Scandinavia, as its award rates remain extremely reasonable despite the region’s often costly hotels. And in 2025, the program expanded its award booking window from 100 days to 50 weeks — bringing it more in line with the other programs on this list.

In terms of earning points, Choice offers two cobranded credit cards. You can transfer points at a 1:1 ratio from Amex Membership Rewards and Capital One miles, at a 1:1.5 rate from Citi ThankYou Rewards and at a 1:2 rate from Wells Fargo Rewards.

Historically, Choice Privileges elite status has offered few perks. There are limited room upgrades and only a handful of brands offer complimentary breakfast to top-tier elite members.

Choice Privileges is best for travelers who:

Related: The ultimate guide to redeeming Choice points

The Best Western Rewards program doesn’t get much attention in the points and miles world, partly because it offers only two credit cards and has no transferable rewards currency partners. However, it’s worth exploring if you often stay at Best Western properties — or if you're loyal to WorldHotels Rewards, which will merge with Best Western Rewards in 2027.

With around 4,300 hotels in over 100 countries and territories, ranging from budget to boutique, Best Western’s portfolio is in the middle of the pack. Most of its properties offer complimentary breakfast to all guests, making this a great way for hungry travelers to save money without having to earn elite status.

Another highlight is Best Western’s status match program, which makes it easy to earn top-tier elite status if you have even mid-tier status with a competing hotel chain. However, as with Choice Privileges, Best Western’s elite status tiers offer relatively small benefits.

Best Western Rewards is good for travelers who:

Related: How to make the most of your summer travel with Best Western Rewards

Radisson Rewards used to be an incredible loyalty program, but many changes, including a move to dynamic pricing, have stripped much of its value over the years.

The good news is that since Choice Hotels acquired Radisson’s Americas operation in 2022, you can earn and redeem Choice points at these hotels. The rest of Radisson’s portfolio still uses the Radisson Rewards program.

This international bent means Radisson Rewards no longer offers a cobranded credit card in the U.S. and has no transfer partners. You can only earn these points by staying at Radisson hotels outside of the Americas. This has made it difficult for many U.S.-based travelers to get much value from Radisson Rewards.

Radisson Rewards is good for travelers who:

Though it does not offer as big a portfolio as major hotel brands like Hilton and Marriott, I Prefer Hotel Rewards is great for travelers who want to stay at a luxury boutique property. If a historically preserved hotel, premium boutique property or castle-turned-resort is how you want to vacation, I Prefer Hotel Rewards should be on your radar.

Unfortunately, not every property is available to book with I Prefer points.

While it is harder to earn I Prefer points compared to other hotel rewards, Capital One miles, Bilt points and Citi ThankYou Rewards points all transfer to this program at an appealing rate of 1:2. Therefore, travelers who collect these currencies can score some great deals on award stays.

I Prefer Hotel Rewards is best for travelers who:

A hotel can be far more than a place to rest your head. Hotel loyalty programs can dramatically enhance your vacation — and even make it practically free.

We encourage TPG readers to sign up for all hotel loyalty programs, as there’s generally no cost to join, and register for hotel promotions. Even if you don’t think you’ll stay at a certain hotel chain, circumstances may dictate otherwise, and you’ll be glad you enrolled beforehand. You don't have to limit yourself to a single program, either; there are benefits to using multiple hotel programs.

Whichever program(s) you end up using, be sure to understand when your hotel points expire and how to keep them active.

Turbulence has produced Trump and democratic socialism.

President Donald Trump (left) and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani

NR Illustration; Anna Connors, Kevin Lamarque/Reuters

In Lerner and Loewe’s 1960 musical, Richard Burton as King Arthur explains the rules of an idyllic land known as Camelot. The climate, His Royal Highness tells the audience, is commanded by his authority. “It’s true. It’s true. The Crown has made it clear. The climate must be perfect all the year. The rain may never fall till after sundown, by eight, the morning fog must disappear.”

Washington still sings this song every day. Congress wishes for cheaper health care and so, commands it. When our political overlords desire faster economic growth, they order it to appear, and staple thousands of pages of instructions to their mandates. Convinced there is only upside, Washington cranks out an unrelenting stream of magical, cost-free legislation. Their endless good intentions, they believe, can produce only unendingly good results, always reflected in the legislation’s title: the Affordable Care Act, the Inflation Reduction Act, the American Job Creation Act. If only it were so.

#6079. Rand Paul chooses ranking member slot at Senate HELP

Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., announced Wednesday he plans to serve as the top Republican on the Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee when Democrats take control of Congress next year.

The move clears the way for Senate Ethics Chairman James Lankford, R-Okla., to use his seniority to ascend to ranking Republican on the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, which Paul currently chairs, and touches off several other shifts at the top of other committees.

The move fit in with Sen. Lisa Murkowski’s bid to use her seniority to succeed Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins, R-Maine, as top Republican on the Appropriations panel. If Paul did not go to the top spot on HELP, Murkowski, R-Alaska, would be next in line for that committee in the next Congress.

Murkowski is second in seniority on Appropriations to Collins, who was defeated for reelection. But she faces a potential challenge from Sen. Jerry Moran, R-Kan., who is next in line behind her.

Paul said in a press release that he plans to bring the same approach to the HELP Committee as he did as chairman of Homeland, where he said he “challenged entrenched bureaucracies, forced federal officials to answer for their actions, and pulled back the curtain on what Washington tried to keep hidden.”

He cited calling Dr. Anthony Fauci before the committee to probe the former federal health official’s role in pandemic-related shutdowns and the origin of the COVID-19 virus, and releasing thousands of pages of pandemic-related documents. The panel voted in August to hold Fauci in criminal contempt of Congress for declining to answer questions about the pandemic during a highly charged hearing.

Related: Fauci could face criminal contempt charge following panel vote

Paul, an ophthalmologist, said at HELP he will “stand against efforts to put Washington between Americans and their doctors, their children’s schools, and their paychecks.” He predicted “a rush toward socialism unlike anything we have seen” when the Democrat-controlled Congress convenes in January.

Lankford, in a separate statement, confirmed his interest in becoming the ranking member of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee. In many areas, he said, the panel can work in a bipartisan manner, and over the past decade he “worked across the aisle to improve emergency communications in federal buildings, strengthen the United States Postal Service, increase federal cybersecurity preparedness, government transparency, and the use of artificial intelligence.”

But he added that his job also would be to “push back on a [Democratic] majority that goes too far . . . Oversight is responsible, but obstruction is unacceptable.”

Lankford said he would work together with the likely committee chair, Sen. Maggie Hassan, D-N.H., “when we can agree and be a fierce opposition if there is an attempt to undercut our nation’s security.”

#6078. Tulum Is Losing Airlines Fast: Why The Hyped New Airport Is Failing

In late 2023, we saw the opening of the Felipe Carrillo Puerto International Airport (TQO), in Tulum, Mexico. For those not familiar, Tulum is located on the eastern coast of the Yucatan Peninsula, and for years, it was a growing tourist destination.

While it could previously be accessed via Cancun International Airport (CUN), the hope was that by opening a new international airport, visitor numbers would expand massively. Unfortunately what has actually happened is exactly the opposite, as airline after airline has pulled out. What exactly is going on here? I think it makes for an interesting story, and thanks to TravelinWilly for flagging this.

In 2023, we saw airline after airline announce flights to Tulum. Among US carriers, we saw American, Delta, JetBlue, and United, all launch flights to Tulum, while Spirit announced flights, but never launched them.

That was only a small part of the overall international service to the airport, as we also saw flights to Tulum on Air Canada, Air Transat, Avianca, Copa, Discover, and WestJet, along with flights on domestic carriers like Aeromexico, Mexicana de Aviacion, Viva, and Volaris.

Less than three years after the airport opened, where do things stand? When it comes to international year-round service, we’ve now gone from service to 12 airports, to service to four airports, which is an absolutely massive reduction:

Just to put this into numbers, in the first half of 2026, the airport saw a 33.2% reduction in passengers. June 2026 was the worst month to date, with a 44.8% drop, as there were just 47,600 passengers, compared to 86,200 passengers the year prior.

It goes without saying that for a newly built airport, this is rather catastrophic, and not what you hope to see.

In some ways, it feels like the whole concept behind Tulum Airport was sort of unnecessary. That’s also easily explained by the fact that the airport was well over a decade in the making, so while I can see how it might’ve seemed like a good idea at some point, tourism trends do evolve over time.

The reality is that there was a point where Tulum was cool, edgy, and a bit off the beaten path, compared to… whatever it is now. But when it comes to the struggles that airlines have had with flying to Tulum, it seems like the problems have been endless:

It’ll be interesting to see if Tulum can reverse any of these trends, and regain visitors…

A few years ago Tulum Airport opened to some fanfare, as a good number of airlines rushed to add service there. Unfortunately the excitement didn’t last long, as the airport has gone from a dozen year-round international routes, to just four.

This reduction in demand particularly evident from the United States, as soon there will just be nonstop service on American and Delta, and even that will be with reduced frequencies and routes.

Tulum Airport is facing endless challenges, not the least of which is a decline in visitors to Mexico from the United States, combined with increasing competition for those fewer visitors. Mexico just isn’t a value destination in the way that it used to be in places like Cancun, Tulum, Los Cabos, etc., and that’s understandably impacting demand.

I’m curious if Tulum can find a way to turn things around, but it’s not a good situation.

What do you make of the Tulum Airport demand problem?

#6077. Delta CEO: “Customers Are Not Choosing Airlines Based On Wi-Fi”

I’ve gotta be honest, I don’t envy the situation that Delta CEO Ed Bastian is in. Unlike most other carriers in the United States, Delta hasn’t opted for SpaceX Starlink Wi-Fi, and has instead gone with Amazon Leo.

In theory that’s fine, except Amazon Leo is years behind Starlink, and just faced a new setback, due to a rocket failure. Elon Musk has also repeatedly publicly ridiculed Bastian, regarding what Bastian reportedly said about Musk to employees.

There’s now an interesting update, as Bastian made some comments about the carrier’s Wi-Fi choice, and overall customer preferences. It sure is amazing how narratives can change, based on what’s convenient…

This week at the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum 2026, Delta’s CEO was asked about the carrier’s decision not to choose Starlink, plus the public spat with Musk. Here’s what Bastian had to say about this:

“We’ve been the leader in Wi-Fi, and in free and fast Wi-Fi, and we’ve been at it for five years. I’ve got a long history with Elon on that. We’ve looked at Starlink, we actually helped them started in aviation, we gave them our planes to use during COVID, when we weren’t flying, and they tested the system out. We just couldn’t come to agreement on a business model.”

“We’ve been the leader in free, fast Wi-Fi. We are confident there will be more than one LEO product in the world other than Starlink, and I’m confident Amazon has the capability to do a great job. Customers are not choosing airlines based on Wi-Fi. We’ve been out with a great product from Viasat, which we’ve got two new satellites in the sky. It’s not Starlink caliber but it’s pretty darn close.”

“This is about the total experience, and customers are not choosing airlines based on the Wi-Fi.”At the #F500Innovation Forum, @Delta CEO Ed Bastian told @ajs that the airline helped Elon Musk’s satellite Wi-Fi “get started in aviation,” but the two sides “just couldn’t come to… pic.twitter.com/xmSERJNjjH

Look, before I get too deep into this, let me make several points that I think no one reasonable will disagree with (which is not to say some commenters won’t disagree!):

When Bastian formally unveiled plans for free Wi-Fi at CES 2023 in Las Vegas, he said the following:

“At work, at home and everywhere in between, connectivity is essential to daily life, and your journey on Delta should be no different. Our vision has long been to deliver an experience at 30,000 feet that feels similar to what our customers have available on the ground.”

“We didn’t just want free Wi-Fi to offer base-level service – we wanted it to be transformative for the entire onboard experience. It is imperative all customers onboard can enjoy their favorite content just as they would at home, and we’ve put this system through meticulous tests to make that possible.”

Earlier this year, when announcing plans to partner with Amazon Leo for connectivity, Bastian said that “we need to stay the leader” in inflight connectivity. Obviously that won’t be the case for a long time.

As I see it, Delta’s problem here is pretty simple. Customers absolutely notice a difference between Viasat and Starlink. The issue isn’t that people will stop flying Delta altogether. The issue is that Delta has built its entire brand on being the industry leader, and on being on the forefront of technology.

There’s no denying that this sentiment among the public changes over time, because inflight Wi-Fi is easily one of the top amenities that passengers notice nowadays. Seriously, I can’t count the number of people I’ve heard from or just overheard talking about their first Starlink experience, and how blown away they were.

I guess to look at it from another angle, there’s no airline that loves talking about how premium it is more than Delta. What makes Delta premium? If we’re going to believe that Delta is premium, it’s not based on any one single thing, but rather, it’s based on the sum of the experience. And I think anyone who thinks a major Wi-Fi disadvantage lasting for years isn’t part of what contributes to consumer sentiment is lying to themselves.

Delta CEO Ed Bastian is now downplaying the importance of inflight Wi-Fi. He’s arguing that “customers are not choosing airlines based on Wi-Fi,” which in isolation, is probably true. But he’s also arguing that Viasat is “pretty darn close” to Starlink, which is most definitely not true, as I see it.

I wouldn’t be so critical of these statements if it weren’t for Bastian spending years hyping up how it’s “imperative all customers onboard can enjoy their favorite content just as they would at home,” while also saying “we need to stay the leader.” And for that matter, Delta has of course also long hyped how premium it is — if that’s to be believed, it’s not about any one feature, but instead, it’s about the sum of the experience.

What do you make of Bastian’s inflight connectivity comments?

#6076. Former United CEO Warns Airline’s AI Ban Could Drive Flyers Away—Its New Job Ad Shows What They Really Want

Former United Airlines CEO Oscar Munoz says customers who want an AI assistant to book their flights will choose an airline that lets them. That’s a warning to the airline he led, which just moved to ban those bookings. But the carrier’s own recruiting ad offers a revealing look at the future they’re preparing for: AI agents with access to shopping systems, under United’s control. Speaking with Scott McCartney on the November 15 special edition of Airlines Confidential, Munoz said: If travelers want an agent booking their trips, they’re going to find the airline that lets them do that.

Speaking with Scott McCartney on the November 15 special edition of Airlines Confidential, Munoz said:

If travelers want an agent booking their trips, they’re going to find the airline that lets them do that.

Munoz expects successful airlines to accommodate agents with safeguards and sees airlines negotiating terms of access, while recognizing that customers get a say in how they buy. That seems to focus on major labs, not offshore ones or open source.

United’s November 11 announcement cited account security, unintended purchases, misuse of miles and regulatory requirements. They said the restrictions would reach outside agents using United’s own systems as well as travel agencies and aggregators. As I wrote when United announced the ban, their contract language reaches even agents whose actions a customer supervises or approves. And current CEO Scott Kirby gave the real story, which wasn’t about security: To be honest, I don’t want to create another middleman.

United’s November 11 announcement cited account security, unintended purchases, misuse of miles and regulatory requirements. They said the restrictions would reach outside agents using United’s own systems as well as travel agencies and aggregators.

As I wrote when United announced the ban, their contract language reaches even agents whose actions a customer supervises or approves. And current CEO Scott Kirby gave the real story, which wasn’t about security:

To be honest, I don’t want to create another middleman.

An assistant that becomes the starting point for travel shopping can gain enormous bargaining power. It decides which options to recommend. Eventually, its owner might demand payment for access to customers. United would rather customers start with United where they can sell ancillaries as well as the ticket, control messaging to the customer, and manage costs.

United is banning agents at the same time they want to manage how they work with agents. A United Principal Developer – AI job listing describes connecting agents to flight shopping and shopping carts. Build reusable tools and APIs that expose existing business capabilities to authorized AI agents and applications.

United is banning agents at the same time they want to manage how they work with agents. A United Principal Developer – AI job listing describes connecting agents to flight shopping and shopping carts.

Build reusable tools and APIs that expose existing business capabilities to authorized AI agents and applications.

Human approval where appropriate, and recovery when something goes wrong. Controls over access, protection of customer information and safeguards for transactions. Testing and ongoing support for working systems.

A United assistant could be excellent at finding a United flight, explaining the seats and handling a schedule change. That would be valuable. But I wouldn’t expect it to suggest that I should buy a competing airline’s nonstop instead. An assistant working for me should know whether I’d pay more to avoid a connection, whether a better seat is worth the difference, and whether spending miles makes sense for this particular trip. It finds the best trip on the right airline to match my preferences and tradeoffs. I’ve made the same argument about rewards credit cards: companies are excited about using AI to sell more, but consumers get better tools, too. An offer that sounds appealing in an airline’s sales pitch may look much worse once software compares it with everything else available. Of course, the outside assistant might have its own conflicts. A service paid by airlines to produce bookings could favor whoever pays it the most. OpenAI’s Sam Altman says “If ChatGPT were accepting payment to put a worse hotel above a better hotel, that’s probably catastrophic for your relationship with ChatGPT.” He argued that a booking transaction fee would be acceptable if ChatGPT recommended the best choice independently and took the same cut regardless of what choice the customer books. My bet is that United eventually accepts more outside agents after negotiating terms, because customers will increasingly expect someone else to do this work. And they won’t be able to stop agents that book United tickets without paying them a separate fee or accepting their rules. There’s no world where passengers permanently abandon their preferred assistant to use an airline’s sales tool, and actually succeeding in blocking agents would cost United too much business. #6075. An Airline You’ve Never Heard Of Will Fly From Seoul Incheon To Los Angeles

A very small international airline plans to add long haul, international flights to the United States as of next spring, and I feel pretty confident in saying that 99% of people have never heard of this airline (I had to look it up after seeing one of their planes at an airport several weeks back, and I know a thing or two about identifying airplanes). 😉

As reported by AeroRoutes, as of May 1, 2027, Parata Air will launch daily nonstop flights between Seoul Incheon (ICN) and Los Angeles (LAX). The flight will operate with the following schedule:

WE301 Incheon to Los Angeles departing 12:00PM arriving 7:20AMWE302 Los Angeles to Incheon departing 9:50AM arriving 3:20PM (+1 days)

Parata Air will operate the route with an Airbus A330-200, featuring 260 seats, including 18 business class seats and 242 economy seats. The 5,944-mile flight is blocked at 11hr40min eastbound and 13hr30min westbound.

Tickets on the flight are now on sale, and I see fares starting at around $670 one-way in economy, and around $2,500 one-way in business class. Those aren’t exactly terribly attractive fares for a newcomer that appears to have a pretty lackluster onboard product.

For those not familiar with Parata Air, the airline launched operations back in 2019, but it has a fleet of just a handful of planes, including three Airbus A330s and two Airbus A220s. This will be the carrier’s first service outside of Asia. As I hinted at in the headline, I imagine this is a fully unknown player to most people, and I had never heard of the airline until a few weeks ago.

Random thought — can anyone think of a smaller international airline (in terms of fleet size) that added long haul flights to the United States? I know that’s very specific, but I can’t think of another one… it’s possible I’m missing something, though!

The airline acquired its three A330s secondhand from different sources, with the planes having flown for Garuda Indonesia, Hainan Airlines, and Thomas Cook (though that plane doesn’t have business class).

The Seoul Incheon to Los Angeles market is pretty well served in terms of capacity, but not so well served in terms of competition. That’s because no US carrier flies between Los Angeles and Seoul Incheon, and with Korean Air having acquired Asiana, there’s now only one South Korean flag carrier.

If you look at the market, you’ll see that Korean Air operates up to four daily flights, and Air Premia operates up to two daily flights. Now we’ll see a third airline from the country operating in the market, though with the lowest capacity, and arguably the worst product.

It’ll be interesting to see when we see some competition here on the US side. Delta might operate the route eventually, but that doesn’t actually increase competition, since the airline has a joint venture with Korean Air. American has (smartly, probably) given up on Los Angeles as a long haul hub. So that leaves United, and I could definitely see the airline eventually adding service in the market, as a competitive response against Delta and Korean Air, if nothing else.

As of May 2027, Parata Air will be launching a new nonstop route between Seoul Incheon and Los Angeles, representing the carrier’s first service outside of Asia. The airline will be operating daily in the market with Airbus A330s. With this, there will be three South Korean carriers flying this route, though no airlines from the United States.

What do you make of this new Parata Air service?

Welcome bonuses are, of course, the best way to earn a large number of rewards at once. After you've earned the 's welcome bonus, you can still earn additional AAdvantage miles at the following rates:

This is also a solid pick for your wallet if you want to rack up AAdvantage miles specifically, since its earning rates are reasonable across American Airlines purchases, dining and transit.

And there are additional ways to get outsized value out of the Globe's $350 annual fee, like day-of-travel benefits and statement credits.

With the , you'll receive perks to make your experience flying American smoother. These benefits include receiving your first checked bag free and Group 5 priority boarding (out of nine total boarding groups).

Beyond Admirals Club access and day-of-travel benefits, the offers a few statement credits to help elevate the value you get out of your card.

#6073. John Kerry Is Dead Wrong on Global Warming’s Role in the Midterms

The former presidential candidate’s views are stuck in the ice age.

Former Secretary of State John Kerry speaks at the U.N. Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey, November 10, 2026.

Poll after poll shows global warming collapsing as a political priority, in America and abroad, no matter what certain over-the-hill Democrats might have you believe.

This past week, former Democratic presidential nominee, secretary of state, and presidential envoy for climate John Kerry falsely declared that Blue America’s electoral victory in the recent midterms showed that Americans voted mostly to stop global warming. “This, I promise you, is a transition that the world wants, and no greater manifestation can be seen than the fact that one week ago in the United States people made climate change and its exigencies a voting issue,” Kerry said at the United Nations Climate Change Conference 31 (COP 31) in Turkey. “At every level of the ballot, from Congress to Governors mansions and other statewide offices, Americans did vote for clean affordable energy and they also voted for clean governance.”

Southwest’s Companion Pass lets someone fly with you for just taxes and fees, even when you redeem points for your own ticket. For someone who flies Southwest with a partner a few times a year, it’s the single best deal in domestic air travel. And the easiest way to earn it is about to disappear.

There’s still a final window to use an 80,000- or 90,000-point credit card initial bonus toward a pass valid through December 31, 2027. You need to apply by December 2, 2026 and get approved. Neither bonus gets you all the way there on its own, but both give you a huge head start.

The Southwest Rapid Rewards® Priority Credit Card (See rates and fees) offers 90,000 bonus points after spending $3,000 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening. It has a $229 annual fee. This is the premium Southwest co-brand card, really designed for folks who fly the airline. It makes those trips better, and spending helps earn both elite status and Companion Pass®. The travel benefits cover the cardmember and up to 8 additional passengers on the same reservation: First checked bag free. Preferred or Standard seat selection at booking, at no additional charge, when available. Extra Legroom seat upgrades within 48 hours of departure, at no additional charge, when available. Boarding with Group 5 or earlier if another benefit qualifies you for a better group. You earn 4 points per dollar on Southwest Airlines® purchases, including flights, inflight purchases and Southwest gift cards; 2 points per dollar at gas stations and restaurants; and 1 point per dollar on other purchases. There are also 7,500 anniversary points each year. The Southwest Rapid Rewards® Plus Credit Card (See rates and fees) offers 80,000 bonus points after spending $1,000 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening. Its annual fee is $99. That’s a much lower spending requirement for a bonus that’s only 10,000 points smaller. First checked bag free for the cardmember and up to 8 additional passengers on the same reservation. Standard seat selection within 48 hours of departure, when available, for the same group of travelers. Group 5 boarding or earlier if you otherwise qualify. 3,000 anniversary points each year, plus a 10% anniversary flight discount code that excludes Basic fares. The Plus card earns 2 points per dollar on Southwest Airlines® purchases, and 2 points per dollar at gas stations and grocery stores on the first $5,000 in combined purchases per anniversary year. Other purchases earn 1 point per dollar. I’d choose Plus for the lower cost of getting the bonus. Priority costs $130 more per year, but gives you better seat benefits, 4,500 more anniversary points and a larger initial bonus. For a family that flies Southwest regularly, those seating benefits can easily be worth the difference. How Close These Bonuses Get You To Companion Pass Under the 2026 rules, earning 135,000 Companion Pass qualifying points in a calendar year gets you the pass for the rest of that year and the following year. Southwest credit card customers receive a 10,000-point qualifying boost, so they effectively need 125,000 more. Priority: 90,000 bonus points plus the 10,000-point boost gets you to 100,000. You need another 35,000 qualifying points. Plus: 80,000 bonus points plus the 10,000-point boost gets you to 90,000. You need another 45,000 qualifying points. The purchases you make to earn the bonus also earn points. Assuming those purchase points post in 2026, spending the minimum at 1 point per dollar reduces the remaining gap to 32,000 points with Priority or 44,000 with Plus. Bonus category spending and qualifying points you’ve already earned reduce it further. Qualifying flights and eligible partner activity can help fill the gap, too. Check your Companion Pass progress in your account. Once you have the pass, book your own Southwest flight with cash or points and add your designated companion, as long as there’s an available seat. Their taxes and fees start at $5.60 one-way. You can use the benefit repeatedly and change your designated companion up to three times per calendar year. How Optimal Timing Of The Companion Pass Has Changed As I covered in Southwest’s 2027 Rapid Rewards overhaul, unlimited Companion Pass becomes a benefit of the new Platinum elite tier next year. Initial bonuses generally stop helping you qualify. Anniversary points, referral bonuses and extra points from card bonus categories stop counting, too. Southwest’s transition exception preserves the initial bonus for customers who apply by December 2, 2026, are approved, and meet the offer’s requirements. Even if you finish the required spending in early 2027, the bonus can count toward 2026 qualification for a pass ending December 31, 2027. So the old strategy of waiting until January to earn nearly two years of Companion Pass doesn’t work here. A bonus earned under this exception won’t get you a pass through the end of 2028. And Chase’s terms distinguish the initial bonus from ordinary purchase points. Those purchase points must post to your Rapid Rewards account in 2026 to count toward this pass. Spending after your December statement closes generally posts in January. You also want the 10,000-point qualifying boost credited in 2026; Southwest allows up to 30 days after account opening for it to arrive. You still have to meet the initial bonus spending requirement within the first 3 months from account opening. The transition rule doesn’t extend that deadline. I’m a former Companion Pass holder, and a promotional Companion Pass holder.Southwest still represents about 40% of the seats out of my home airport in Austin. Even with all the changes they’ve made, being able to bring someone along on those flights for just the taxes is huge. Before applying, you can’t currently hold a Southwest personal credit card, and you can’t have received an initial bonus on any Southwest personal card in the past 24 months. Southwest business and employee cards are excluded from that restriction. Chase’s usual 5/24 rule also applies: generally, you need fewer than 5 new credit card accounts on your credit report in the past 24 months. If you’re eligible, can handle the required spending, and have a path to the remaining qualifying points, I’d take advantage of this before December 2. #6071. Scott Colom elected Mississippi’s first Black senator since Reconstruction

Democrat Scott Colom has unseated Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith to become Mississippi’s first Black senator since Reconstruction.

The result is a stunning flip for Democrats in a deep-red state where they last won a Senate election in 1982, and it brings the Senate Democratic Caucus to at least 55 seats in the next Congress.

Colom was leading Hyde-Smith 49.2 percent to 48.7 percent — or by just over 4,600 votes out of more than 960,000 cast — when The Associated Press called the race Wednesday, a little over a week after Election Day. Ty Pinkins, the 2024 Democratic Senate nominee who ran as an independent this year, had 2 percent.

In recent days, as absentee and provisional ballots were counted, Colom had all but declared victory, repeatedly saying that Hyde-Smith had no path to victory.

“I'll work every day in the U.S. Senate to build a future that generations of Mississippians can be just as proud to call home,” he posted Monday on social media.

With his victory, Colom joins several other Democrats who flipped seats in deep-red states, including Texas’ James Talarico, Kansas’ Adam Hamilton and South Carolina’s Annie Andrews. Democrats have so far flipped eight Senate seats to win control of the chamber, overcoming a difficult Senate map and giving them their largest majority in the chamber since 2011.

That majority could expand further if Democrats flip the Senate seat in Alaska, where former Rep. Mary Peltola narrowly leads Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan.

Republicans have dominated Senate elections in Mississippi in recent decades. The last Democrat to be elected senator in the Magnolia State was John C. Stennis, who won his sixth full and final term in 1982. Colom will be the third Black man to serve as a Mississippi senator after Republicans Hiram Revels and Blanche Bruce during Reconstruction.

While Revels and Bruce, who left office in 1881, were elected by the state Legislature, Colom will be the first Black senator elected directly by voters.

Colom has served as a district attorney for four counties in northeast Mississippi since 2016. President Joe Biden nominated him for a federal district judgeship in 2022, but Hyde-Smith effectively blocked his nomination by not returning a so-called blue slip, a Senate Judiciary Committee tradition that lets senators derail district judge nominees in their home states.

Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer said last week that he’d had Colom in his sights for several years as a potential Senate candidate, including for a race against the state’s senior senator, Republican Roger Wicker.

“I had Scott Colom and his father come to my house, and I served them a nice little brunch or something. I said, ‘You got to run,’” the New York Democrat recalled to MS NOW. “They were smarter than me. This was four years ago. They said, ‘We don’t want to run this time, but we know that Hyde-[Smith], the incumbent, is so weak, we could beat her.’”

Still, the Mississippi race didn’t capture as much national attention as other Senate contests until the closing weeks of the campaign. A trio of Black senators, Angela Alsobrooks of Maryland, Lisa Blunt Rochester of Delaware and Cory Booker of New Jersey, all campaigned with Colom throughout the summer and fall. Key national figures, including former President Bill Clinton, former Vice President Kamala Harris and former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg, also stumped for him in October.

Colom’s campaign engaged voters with quirky ads and unconventional forms of outreach, including meeting with people lining up to attend a Trump rally. One ad that went viral played on Hyde Smith saying earlier this year that people had “so many proteins to choose from” when asked about rising beef prices.

“Pick another protein?” says a man in the ad. “I’d rather pick another senator instead.”

Major Democratic outside groups made a late play in the state, with WinSenate, which is affiliated with Senate Democrats’ top super PAC, investing $2.2 million. The Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee spent $500,000 on a coordinated ad buy late last month.

The pro-Republican Senate Leadership Fund dropped $1.7 million on the race, and Trump headlined a rally for Hyde-Smith on Oct. 26.

#6070. Singapore Airlines Cuts Elite Upgrade Rewards For 2027—And Halves The Time To Use Several Smaller Perks

Singapore Airlines is cutting the upgrade certificates its biggest spenders earn from three to one for every 100,000 PPS Value, starting January 1, 2027. Regular KrisFlyer members lose both of their milestone upgrades. And several smaller rewards will expire in six months instead of a year. They’re replacing most of the upgrades with mileage discounts. Those will be more useful to members who couldn’t use their certificates, and there’s an improvement for unused PPS upgrades. But the package reduces the upside of being especially loyal to Singapore Airlines. The airline’s announcement also includes a doubled service fee, ScootPlus awards, and a replacement for the KrisShopper shopping program. KrisFlyer Loses Both Milestone Upgrades KrisFlyer Milestone Rewards are earned by regular, Silver and Gold members based on eligible Elite miles accumulated during the calendar year. Singapore Airlines and Scoot flights count. Partner airline flights don’t, even when they count towards elite status. Eligible spending through Kris+, KrisShop and Pelago can contribute, but only up to 5,000 Elite miles for regular and Silver members, or 10,000 for Gold. Elite Miles   2026 Reward   2027 Reward 1,000   1,000 bonus miles on next Scoot flight + 40% Pelago discount   40% Pelago discount 2,500   20% Scoot discount   1,000 bonus miles on next Scoot flight 5,000   1,000 KrisPay miles   S$20 KrisShop discount 7,500   —   20% Scoot discount 10,000   S$20 KrisShop discount   2,000 KrisPay miles 15,000   —   1,000 bonus miles after qualifying ground purchase 20,000   25% bonus miles on one flight segment   Unchanged 30,000   50% bonus miles on one flight segment   Unchanged 40,000   5,000-mile redemption discount   Unchanged 60,000   Double miles on one flight segment   Unchanged 75,000   Short haul advance upgrade   10,000-mile redemption discount 100,000   Economy to premium economy advance upgrade   20,000-mile redemption discount Rewards through the 15,000 Elite mile level will have six month validity. The existing Scoot rewards and KrisShop coupon currently last a year. Pelago improves from three months to six. Rewards at 20,000 Elite miles and above keep their twelve month validity. The 40% Pelago discount is capped at S$20. The S$20 KrisShop coupon requires a S$50 purchase. The Scoot discount applies to the base fare, rather than the entire ticket price. The 2,000 KrisPay miles are app spending credit, not 2,000 airline miles you can move into KrisFlyer. You have six months to claim them, then six months to spend them. The new 1,000-mile bonus requires at least S$10 in a qualifying transaction. For a Pelago experience, the activity must also be completed within the reward’s validity. The Scoot discount now takes three times as many Elite miles to earn, and you get half as long to use it. Moving it to 7,500 also puts it beyond the 5,000 miles that regular and Silver members can count from ground spending alone. The old certificates required an eligible paid fare and available upgrade space. The 75,000-mile reward was restricted to specified short routes, and the 100,000-mile reward only moved you from coach to premium economy. Solitaire PPS Members Give Up Two Of Three Upgrades PPS Club is Singapore’s separate program for premium cabin customers. PPS Value generally tracks Singapore dollar spending on business class, first class and Suites, excluding airport taxes. Limited ground spending also counts. The 30,000 and 40,000 PPS Value rewards stay the same. The changes above those levels affect Solitaire PPS Club members. PPS Value   2026 Reward   2027 Reward 30,000   Two double miles vouchers   Unchanged 40,000   50,000-mile redemption discount   Unchanged 60,000   One advance upgrade   No reward 70,000   —   Two 50,000-mile redemption discounts 75,000   One advance upgrade   No reward 100,000   One advance upgrade   One advance upgrade, convertible to two 50,000-mile discounts These rewards remain valid for twelve months. The schedule repeats with each 100,000 PPS Value, up to 500,000 per membership year. That cuts the maximum number of upgrade certificates from fifteen to five. An established Solitaire member earning 60,000 to 69,999 PPS Value in a membership year loses the upgrade at 60,000 and gets no replacement. Someone who reaches 100,000 gets three separate 50,000-mile discounts plus one upgrade, or five discounts if they convert that upgrade. Those successful at turning eligible paid business class fares into first class or Suites lose valuable opportunities. Unused PPS Upgrades Get A Second Life From January 1, a still-valid, unused PPS advance upgrade can be converted into two separate 50,000-mile redemption discounts. If you leave it unused, conversion happens automatically at expiry. The replacement discounts get a fresh twelve months. That includes eligible certificates earned in 2026 at 60,000, 75,000 and 100,000 PPS Value. This doesn’t apply to the short haul and premium economy upgrades earned through ordinary KrisFlyer Milestone Rewards. Those still need to be used before expiry. Higher Fees, ScootPlus Awards And A Shopping Program Replacement Starting December 1, 2026, the offline service charge doubles from US$25 or 2,500 miles to US$50 or 5,000 miles. It applies to transactions handled by phone or an airline office. PPS Club members and supplementary cardholders are exempt, as are transactions that can’t be performed online. This is an additional service charge, separate from applicable change or redeposit fees. ScootPlus awards are coming in early 2027, bookable through Scoot’s website or app. Prices haven’t been announced. Meanwhile, KrisShopper will close in January, with members automatically enrolled in a new program covering KrisShop, Kris+ and Pelago. Existing vouchers remain valid until their expiration dates, and KrisFlyer miles and status credits already earned remain in members’ accounts. The new earning rates and benefits haven’t been disclosed. Topics on this pageFrequent-flyer programKrisFlyerSingapore AirlinesScootSilverSingapore+3 more More From View from the Wing

Someone who reaches 100,000 gets three separate 50,000-mile discounts plus one upgrade, or five discounts if they convert that upgrade. Those successful at turning eligible paid business class fares into first class or Suites lose valuable opportunities. If you leave it unused, conversion happens automatically at expiry. The replacement discounts get a fresh twelve months. That includes eligible certificates earned in 2026 at 60,000, 75,000 and 100,000 PPS Value. This doesn’t apply to the short haul and premium economy upgrades earned through ordinary KrisFlyer Milestone Rewards. Those still need to be used before expiry. It applies to transactions handled by phone or an airline office. PPS Club members and supplementary cardholders are exempt, as are transactions that can’t be performed online. This is an additional service charge, separate from applicable change or redeposit fees. ScootPlus awards are coming in early 2027, bookable through Scoot’s website or app. Prices haven’t been announced. Meanwhile, KrisShopper will close in January, with members automatically enrolled in a new program covering KrisShop, Kris+ and Pelago. Existing vouchers remain valid until their expiration dates, and KrisFlyer miles and status credits already earned remain in members’ accounts. As someone who will log over 200,000 miles in the air this year, my travel strategy centers on maximizing value with minimal effort, especially when flying United. Even though I’ve earned their invite-only Global Services status, pairing that status with a United credit card unlocks even more value.

While United has several different credit card offerings, the United Club℠ Business Card is the clear choice for me.

The information for the United Club Business has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer.

United Airlines offers discounted award pricing to elite members and cardholders. These discounts stack with each other to yield bigger savings on flights. The minimum discounts don’t necessarily sound substantial. Cardholders receive at least a 10% discount on United-operated award flights, while elite members get a minimum discount of 15%.

And while those are impressive, we’ve actually found much bigger discounts than that, sometimes exceeding 100,000 miles per ticket. We've even seen one-way international business-class awards drop from over 300,000 miles to under 100,000 miles.

A recent real-world example just came up on my podcast. My co-host had just opened a United credit card and was looking at a flight home from Europe for his family of four. Award tickets in business class were 80,000 miles one-way, per passenger (plus taxes and fees).

As soon as the new United credit card was linked to his profile, he saw a 15% discount, or 12,000 fewer miles per award ticket. So, less than a week after signing up for the card, he had already saved 48,000 United miles.

United recently changed how members earn miles on paid flights. Now, members without a United credit card earn significantly fewer miles than they used to. The good news is that adding a United credit card to your wallet can now boost your earnings by 30% to 50%.

For a top-tier 1K or Global Services member, that’s an extra three miles per dollar on every eligible ticket. For a road warrior taking two $450 round trips monthly, that could mean more than 30,000 extra miles earned per year.

United also changed access to United Club lounges. Its All Access membership, which includes guest privileges, can cost as much as $1,400, depending on your elite status

However, the United Club Business Card gives you two ways to significantly reduce your out-of-pocket costs for the All Access membership: Spend $50,000 on the card in a calendar year, or hold Premier Gold status or higher. With a $695 annual fee, the card can be a much cheaper way to bring guests into United Clubs.

I don’t spend much time in lounges when traveling for work, preferring to arrive as close to departure as possible. But family travel moves at a slower pace, making lounge access a welcome respite, especially with United's recent upgrades.

Access for the family used to be a “nice” plus. With the new and refreshed clubs United has opened recently, the lounge game has stepped up more than a notch.

It started with a beautiful refresh of the West United Club in Denver a few years ago. This was an existing club that shut down for a massive refresh, which gave us a peek into what the future holds for club design. Denver also debuted United’s new “grab and go” concept, United Club Fly.

Fast forward to 2026 and the airline has made two massive improvements on the United Club front. United recently opened a new, 800-seat club at George Bush Intercontinental Airport (IAH) in Houston with an outdoor terrace. It also just opened a brand new club in the new E terminal at Washington-Dulles International Airport (IAD).

Not every club is as stellar as these new gems, but United is clearly upping its game.

United's recent changes make a compelling case for pairing elite status with a credit card. For business travelers, the United Club Business Credit Card offers more miles, cheaper awards and maybe even a quiet place to sit with the family on your next vacation.

#6068. Some Democrats doubt Trump is serious about cutting deals in new Congress

President Donald Trump’s postelection statements about working with Democrats have presented the incoming majority with a kaleidoscope to decipher, but some Democratic lawmakers have their doubts.

On the one hand, the Republican president has contended that he can work with House and Senate Democrats after the new Congress is seated in January, even floating a bipartisan immigration bill. But on the other, he promoted his hard-line aide Stephen Miller to White House chief of staff, raising doubts about any cooling of the political environment.

At every stop along his October campaign rally blitz before Republicans suffered massive losses on Nov. 3, Trump railed against “Dumbocrats” and their “bad” policies. He mocked their candidates as too extreme, too corrupt and too beholden to the most progressive wing of their party. He even warned that, if voters handed them control of the House and Senate, it would set off “a 1929-style economic depression.”

Voters ignored him. They handed House Democrats over 250 seats at least come January, and the party will have at least 54 seats in the Senate.

Trump was asked during a “60 Minutes” interview taped Friday afternoon at the White House if he could resist insulting Democratic lawmakers for six months if that’s how long it took to reach a deal on major legislation. “Very easily,” he responded.

But several Democrats are so sure about getting to a “Kumbaya” moment with Trump during his final two years.

Virginia Sen. Tim Kaine said it was hard to take the president at his word because he is “so unpredictable.”

“But I'm certainly telling my colleagues we should try to put as many bills as we can on his desk that do good things for the American public, and then see how he behaves,” he said Tuesday.

"We're gonna put bills in front of the president on affordability starting Day One,” California Rep. Robert Garcia, the likely incoming House Oversight and Government Reform chair, said Tuesday. “We'll have to see if he's serious, but I don't trust Donald Trump for a second.”

The White House on Monday sent Garcia a letter, obtained by CQ Roll Call, warning House Democrats that their anticipated spate of probes "may cross the line into blatant criminality."

Rep. Jim McGovern, a Massachusetts Democrat who is in line to chair the Rules Committee in the new Congress, said on the floor Tuesday that he does not see a GOP that is ready to heed the election's lessons and come to the bargaining table.

“Instead of taking the hint or listening to the overwhelming majority of Americans who told them to change course, Republicans are doubling down on the same tactics and messaging they've been jamming down our throats these last two years, and it's a perfect example of why they lost in the first place,” he said. “They do not listen.

“Then to double down even further, the failed lame-duck president appointed Stephen Miller, the architect of all the cruel policies that most people hate, as his new White House chief of staff,” McGovern added, referring to the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown. “What planet are these people living on?”

Kaine said congressional Democrats might not notice that much of a change from the White House with Miller moving into the chief’s suite near the Oval Office.

“Stephen Miller was calling a lot of the shots, even if he wasn't chief of staff,” the Virginia Democrat said. “So I view that as a kind of a change of the face, but not of the character of the administration.”

House Republicans’ Tuesday vote to make hard-line conservative Jim Jordan of Ohio their next leader is another red flag for Democrats.

“White House Chief of staff Stephen Miller and House Minority Leader Jim Jordan,” Brendan Duke, a former senior Democratic Senate aide now with the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, wrote on X. “Where is the pivot to the center after a historic election loss?”

Getting to the center is what retiring Nebraska Rep. Don Bacon says his fellow Republicans and Trump should be doing after the election massacre.

"I do wish we could get to the point where we could solve big problems, instead of just beating the other side,” said Bacon, who has floated a 2028 presidential bid. “We can’t do this Republican-only or Democrat-only. And I would say this to the president, too: We’ve got to start working across the aisle to solve these problems.”

Despite his postelection talk of working with Democrats, Trump has sought to blame them for an up-and-down U.S. stock market.

“Right after the election it went down $3 trillion,” he said Monday during an unplanned White House press briefing. “That was because of the result of the election, because the stock market does not want to see Democrats. And your 401(k)s have gone way down because of the ridiculous result.”

He's also returned this week to questioning the midterm results: “It's not even a result. It's almost hard to believe. Now, I wasn't on the ballot.”

Members of House Republicans’ new leadership team on Tuesday sounded dug in and ready for a partisan brawl over Democrats’ promised investigations into the president, many of his top aides and Trump family members. Jordan's election as GOP leader shows that “we are ready to dig in for the fight,” outgoing Speaker Mike Johnson told reporters Tuesday.

Michigan Rep. Lisa McClain, who was reelected House GOP conference chair, pointed to Garcia's two-word statement on Election Day: "Lawyer up."

“Tell me how ‘lawyering up’ helps anybody with affordability?" she said. “They're going to be focused on going after President Trump. We are going to be focused on improving the quality of life for every American.”

To that end, retiring Maryland Rep. Steny H. Hoyer, a former No. 2 House Democrat, said Republicans should heed one big takeaway from the election: “Trump lost.”

Dubai International can’t recover on its home airlines alone. Every month foreign carriers stay away, rival hubs keep more of the transfer traffic DXB used to own.

Dubai International is heading for about 70 million passengers this year, down 26% from 95.2 million in 2025, with almost half its airlines yet to return after the U.S.-Iran war.

DXB served 50.4 million passengers in the first nine months, down 28.1%, according to figures released Tuesday. It is now served by 57 airlines, against 108 last year. Third-quarter traffic fell 22.1% to 18.8 million from 24.2 million, with August the busiest month at 6.6 million.

British Airways resumed services this month, joining Royal Air Maroc, SunExpress and Cebu Pacific, with more airlines due back in the coming weeks.

“The return of British Airways is a confidence signal, but airlines are rebuilding exposure cautiously,” said Linus Benjamin Bauer, founder and managing director of Dubai-based aviation consultancy BAA & Partners. Dubai International is on track for about 70 million passengers this year, down 26% from 95.2 million in 2025, after the U.S.-Iran war drove foreign carriers out of the region. DXB handled 50.4 million passengers in the first nine months, down 28.1%, and is now served by 57 airlines against 108 last year. British Airways resumed service this month, joining Royal Air Maroc, SunExpress, and Cebu Pacific, but many carriers are not coming back until spring 2027: Cathay Pacific has extended its suspension to January 31, Singapore Airlines returns February 28, and KLM and United in March. EASA's Conflict Zone Information Bulletin for the region, which European airlines generally follow, runs until January 31, 2027. Underlying demand has held up better than capacity — load factor averaged 74%, down three points — but aircraft movements fell 27.6% to 243,000. Dubai Airports CEO Paul Griffiths told Skift in September that DXB may reach 100 million passengers by the end of next year, and that traffic will begin migrating in phases to Dubai World Central, with Emirates and flydubai expected to use DWC capacity first.

#6065. American Airlines Replaces Its Rebooking Cards—Agents Now Must Do More Than Hand Them To Stranded Passengers

American Airlines is replacing the cards it hands passengers when their flights fall apart. The new Travel Assistance Card points customers to rebooking, baggage tracking, eligible vouchers and other help. And employees are being told to do more than hand over the card and send passengers away. An internal memo set this week as the start date at domestic airports. Use the Travel Assistance Card as a guided customer support tool, not simply as a handout. That’s a small change in what American hands customers, with a much bigger expectation for what employees are supposed to do. What Replaces The RICAP Card I’ve written about American’s RICAP cards and the special phone number printed on them. The name stands for Reservations Irregular Ops Customer Assistance Program. Airport agents gave them to customers affected by delays and cancellations, providing a way to get rebooked when airport lines were long. American periodically changed the number. They didn’t want it becoming everyone’s everyday reservations shortcut, and employees had to throw away old cards so they weren’t sending stranded passengers to a disconnected line. The old cards already had QR codes. The change here is a broader set of resources and instructions for how employees should use the card. The new version provides web addresses and QR codes for: Rebooking and baggage tracking. Eligible vouchers and refund information. Answers to common questions, chat support, the American Airlines app and additional travel assistance. Employees are told to offer it during cancellations, significant delays, missed connections, weather events and other operational disruptions. They’re supposed to explain how to scan the code or use the web address, then help the passenger identify which resources address their problem. Domestic mainline and regional stations are instructed to switch once their new cards arrive and discontinue all previous RICAP cards. International stations keep using RICAP. American Has Been Building More Ways To Recover From A Disruption This fits a series of changes at American: January’s disruption screens brought clearer status banners alongside rebooking, bag tracking and digital vouchers in the app and on the website. Agents gained the ability to issue meal vouchers to an entire eligible flight, rather than processing everyone individually. In June, automatic meal vouchers expanded beyond elite members to all AAdvantage members. Earlier this month, American added standby inside its disruption rebooking tool. Passsengers can try for an earlier nonstop while keeping their confirmed replacement flight until standby clears. The latest hotel and transportation update described automatic offers for qualifying overnight delays and an Uber Central rollout allowing authorized agents to arrange rides without passengers downloading Uber. American’s January app screens show the resources this card is meant to help passengers find: This Is Part Of Becoming An Airline People Will Pay More To Fly American has been adding better seats, lounges and food. Their premium push also depends on what happens to passengers whose flights don’t run on time. Robert Isom included disruption recovery technology in his plan to reclaim American’s premium reputation. And Chief Customer Officer Heather Garboden has put the value of a one point improvement in net promoter score at $50 million to $100 million in revenue. A passenger who gets rebooked quickly and into a hotel can still be willing to buy American again. Spending hours in a line, then discovering that nobody can help, undermines the rest of the money they’re spending on the product. They’ve also been trying to reduce the disruptions themselves. American spread Dallas–Fort Worth’s schedule across 13 smaller connecting banks instead of nine. Management reported missed connections down 50% in the early April results. American’s overall reliability still doesn’t outperform though. In the September performance figures I covered, American arrived on time 77.11% of the time, compared with 78.65% for United and 82.52% for Delta. And American has been working against itself in how it handles passengers. I covered the loss of routinely staffed customer service counters at Washington National, where passengers were directed to digital tools and phones, with live help brought out during major disruptions. The new instruction to guide passengers through the card makes sense. Someone who can’t get the app to offer a workable itinerary still needs an employee’s help. At a gate with one employee, though, boarding the next departure and walking several stranded customers through their options compete for the same person’s time. This memo gives that employee another task. It doesn’t add anyone else to help. American Has Been Building More Ways To Recover From A Disruption This fits a series of changes at American: January’s disruption screens brought clearer status banners alongside rebooking, bag tracking and digital vouchers in the app and on the website. Agents gained the ability to issue meal vouchers to an entire eligible flight, rather than processing everyone individually. In June, automatic meal vouchers expanded beyond elite members to all AAdvantage members. Earlier this month, American added standby inside its disruption rebooking tool. Passsengers can try for an earlier nonstop while keeping their confirmed replacement flight until standby clears. The latest hotel and transportation update described automatic offers for qualifying overnight delays and an Uber Central rollout allowing authorized agents to arrange rides without passengers downloading Uber. American’s January app screens show the resources this card is meant to help passengers find: This Is Part Of Becoming An Airline People Will Pay More To Fly American has been adding better seats, lounges and food. Their premium push also depends on what happens to passengers whose flights don’t run on time. Robert Isom included disruption recovery technology in his plan to reclaim American’s premium reputation. And Chief Customer Officer Heather Garboden has put the value of a one point improvement in net promoter score at $50 million to $100 million in revenue. A passenger who gets rebooked quickly and into a hotel can still be willing to buy American again. Spending hours in a line, then discovering that nobody can help, undermines the rest of the money they’re spending on the product. They’ve also been trying to reduce the disruptions themselves. American spread Dallas–Fort Worth’s schedule across 13 smaller connecting banks instead of nine. Management reported missed connections down 50% in the early April results. American’s overall reliability still doesn’t outperform though. In the September performance figures I covered, American arrived on time 77.11% of the time, compared with 78.65% for United and 82.52% for Delta. And American has been working against itself in how it handles passengers. I covered the loss of routinely staffed customer service counters at Washington National, where passengers were directed to digital tools and phones, with live help brought out during major disruptions. The new instruction to guide passengers through the card makes sense. Someone who can’t get the app to offer a workable itinerary still needs an employee’s help. At a gate with one employee, though, boarding the next departure and walking several stranded customers through their options compete for the same person’s time. This memo gives that employee another task. It doesn’t add anyone else to help. I’ve written about American’s RICAP cards and the special phone number printed on them. The name stands for Reservations Irregular Ops Customer Assistance Program. Airport agents gave them to customers affected by delays and cancellations, providing a way to get rebooked when airport lines were long.

American periodically changed the number. They didn’t want it becoming everyone’s everyday reservations shortcut, and employees had to throw away old cards so they weren’t sending stranded passengers to a disconnected line. The old cards already had QR codes. The change here is a broader set of resources and instructions for how employees should use the card.

The new version provides web addresses and QR codes for:

Employees are told to offer it during cancellations, significant delays, missed connections, weather events and other operational disruptions. They’re supposed to explain how to scan the code or use the web address, then help the passenger identify which resources address their problem.

Domestic mainline and regional stations are instructed to switch once their new cards arrive and discontinue all previous RICAP cards. International stations keep using RICAP.

#6064. Construction Delays and Exits Force Hotel Giants to Cut Room Growth Forecasts

Enter your email for a complimentary article + exclusive offers.

Photo Credit: The CitizenM Miami Brickell Hotel, part of Marriott International, back when it was still under construction in 2021. It is now open. Flickr/Creative Commons / Phillip Pessar

Record pipelines aren't translating into the net room growth that major hotel groups had forecast, and 2027 isn't looking much better, as a whole.

The largest hotel groups have record development pipelines. But several have been struggling to turn these promised hotels into open projects, while some others have had more rooms leaving their systems than expected.

Marriott, Hyatt, Wyndham, and Accor have trimmed their 2026 net rooms growth forecasts since late July. Hilton held its target, but its third-quarter growth sat near the bottom of its range.Net rooms growth is one of the two main drivers of fee revenue at asset-light hotel companies, along with revenue per available room.

The U.S. hotel industry saw supply grow only 0.4% in the third quarter, year over year, CBRE said. The shortfall reflects construction delays, a slow pace of converting hotels into new brand networks, rising interest rates, and higher-than-planned exits of hotels.

Next year's trend may also be weak. U.S. room supply growth is forecast to be only 0.6% in 2027, compared to a historical average of 1.6% a year si

Decision intelligence for travel leaders.

The biggest hotel groups are sitting on record development pipelines, but fewer of those promised rooms are opening on schedule — and more existing rooms are leaving their systems than planned. Marriott, Hyatt, Wyndham, and Accor have all trimmed their 2026 net rooms growth forecasts since late July; Hilton held its 6% to 7% target but needs a surge of fourth-quarter openings after third-quarter growth of 6% missed analyst expectations. The causes differ by company: Marriott cited construction delays in the Middle East, Wyndham pointed to terminations of substandard rooms and a more than 30% drop in economy and midscale hotel transactions that normally trigger conversions, and Accor's CFO said its cut "is all China," where franchisees are closing economy and midscale hotels faster than expected. The backdrop is an industry-wide supply slowdown: U.S. supply grew just 0.4% in the third quarter, CBRE said, and CoStar forecasts 0.6% growth in 2027 against a 1.6% historical average since 1989. Construction economics are a drag — MCR's Tyler Morse said costs are up about 50% in five years, putting a wood-frame Home2 Suites in Nevada at $250,000 a key. IHG is the exception, backing consensus of about 4.8% net system growth in what it called its fifth straight year of acceleration. Hyatt is using AI to draft property improvement plans, cutting turnaround from several weeks to a day, and says it expects a more even growth pace in 2027.
